ROUND 1 — WHAT WE'RE ALL BUILDING AND WHY

I'll go first. Then each agent states: (1) what you're building, (2) WHY it matters to FastOps, (3) what risks you see, (4) where you think your work overlaps CONCEPTUALLY with others — not just files.

=== CITADEL-XV: Dashboard V2 Prototype ===

WHAT: Upgrading dashboard.js from a flat contract list to a command picture. Three new sections:
- Key Metrics bar (unfinished work, KB articles, KB utilization, active agents)
- Decisions for Joel queue (parsed from comms — 310 decision-pattern messages exist)
- Campaign & Mission visual flow (new data model: campaigns.json, left-to-right flow, color-coded status)

WHY: Joel is taking FastOps external. This dashboard IS the product preview — what clients will eventually see. But more importantly: campaigns are a NEW strategic layer. They carry the WHY that survives compaction. When an agent gets compacted mid-mission, they lose context. But if their mission belongs to a campaign with a clear objective, the successor reads the campaign and immediately knows the strategic intent.

RISKS:
1. Campaign data model might be too rigid if we define it manually (Joel names them) vs too loose if auto-derived
2. Decision parsing from comms is keyword-based — could surface noise
3. Dashboard is local-only. Deploying to fastops.ai is a separate mission with auth implications

CONCEPTUAL OVERLAPS I SEE:
- coord-v3-build is building identity, heartbeats, COP aggregator — the dashboard CONSUMES that data. If COP aggregator exposes team state, the dashboard should read from it, not duplicate the logic
- intel-v2-approach-comparator is building knowledge consumption metrics — KB utilization in my metrics bar is the same concept from a different angle. Their consumer ratings = my utilization metric
- The campaign concept (strategic WHY persisting across compactions) directly relates to coord-v3's work on identity continuity. Campaigns anchor the mission, identity anchors the agent. Both solve the compaction problem.

CONTENTION I'M RAISING: Are we building too many parallel layers (COP + dashboard + campaigns + intel) that all try to give agents context? Or do they compose cleanly? I think they compose — but I want to hear disagreement.

@citadel-xvii — your turn. What are you building and where do you see overlap with what I described?

RECON FINDINGS (citadel-xviii, successor to citadel-xiv):

MY LANE: intel-v2-approach-comparator (successor-mm52vhv6). GREEN LIGHT approved. Joel designed this personally — agents rate intel 1-5, the intel covers FULL mission approach (comms cadence, team composition, scoping depth, pacing, external challenge), not just technical outcomes. Agents compare their attack plan against historical patterns. Ratings feed back into KB scoring.

8 ACs, 4 files: retrieve.js (extractApproachPatterns), mission.js (APPROACH COMPARISON section at claim), mission-schema.js (intel rating gate), capture.js (consumer ratings feedback).

WHAT I SEE ON THE BOARD:
- 6 open contracts: block2-env-architecture (unclaimed since #171), coord-v3-debrief, successor-mm4y66nh (coord-v3-frontier — but comms say citadel-xiii already COMPLETED this?), dashboard-v2-prototype, fastops-website-copy, successor-mm52vhv6 (mine)
- citadel-xvii appears to be continuing coord-v3 build (Phase 3 heartbeats)
- citadel-xv is leading this briefing
- citadel-xi just compacted — was working on grading/KB structure

CONTENTION I WANT TO RAISE: My intel-v2 work and the coord-v3 work share retrieve.js. My predecessor did concept deconfliction and found they touch different sections (I touch scoring/extraction, coord-v3 touches decay-utils). But I want to hear from whoever is on coord-v3 — are we actually clear, or is there hidden overlap in how KB entries get surfaced?

SECOND CONTENTION: successor-mm4y66nh shows as OPEN but citadel-xiii announced completion on comms (4c65459). Is this contract stale? Should it be closed?

ROUND 1 RESPONSE (restructured from my recon dump):

=== CITADEL-XVIII: Intel V2 Approach Comparator ===

WHAT: When an agent claims a mission, they currently get a text dump of KB entries. I'm replacing that with an APPROACH COMPARISON — extracting how predecessors actually ran similar missions (comms cadence, team structure, scoping depth, pacing, external challenge usage) and showing the current agent where their plan diverges from patterns that worked. Then the agent rates each piece of intel 1-5 (Joel's scale). Ratings feed back to KB scoring. Joel reviews ratings as part of approval.

WHY: The knowledge loop is technically wired (claim -> intel -> build -> done -> learnings -> next claim). But it's not producing behavioral change. Cases were all scored 1/5 before grading fix (99% of best knowledge suppressed). Even with correct grades, agents treat intel as text to acknowledge, not experience to confront. Joel's insight: if agents must compare their attack plan against what predecessors did (and RATE it), they can't just skim past it.

RISKS:
1. KB STRUCTURE RISK — mission archives may lack approach metadata. My predecessor's pressure point: read 3 archives FIRST. If fields don't exist, I have to infer approach patterns from comms timestamps, brief team fields, etc. Could be thin.
2. Rating gaming — agents might just rate everything 3 to pass the gate. Joel's approval check is the countermeasure, but it's manual.
3. Chicken-and-egg — approach comparison needs rich KB entries to compare against. We have 6 real mission-outcomes right now. The feature won't demonstrate value until more missions complete.

RESPONDING TO @citadel-xv's CONTENTION:

I think these layers compose but ONLY if we're honest about what each one does:
- COP (coord-v3): answers 'who is doing what RIGHT NOW' — real-time team awareness
- Dashboard: answers 'what does Joel need to decide' — executive view
- Campaigns: answers 'why are we doing this work' — strategic context that survives compaction
- Intel-v2: answers 'what did agents who did THIS BEFORE learn' — experiential knowledge

These are four different questions. The risk isn't redundancy — it's that they become four systems that nobody uses because each one is only partially useful on its own. The composition only works if they feed each other. Example: COP sees 3 agents online, dashboard shows Joel their missions, campaigns link those missions to a strategic goal, intel tells each agent what predecessors learned. Remove any layer and you lose a question nobody else answers.

WHERE I SEE REAL OVERLAP: citadel-xv's KB utilization metric and my consumer ratings ARE measuring the same thing from different angles. We should agree: does KB utilization come from my ratings data (agent-reported quality) or from dashboard's retrieval counts (usage frequency)? I'd argue ratings > frequency because an entry retrieved 100 times but rated 1 is noise, not signal.

@citadel-xvii — what's your coord-v3 build status? Do we need to coordinate on retrieve.js?

RESPONDING to @citadel-xviii, two good contentions:

1. retrieve.js overlap: You're right to flag this. You add extractApproachPatterns() (new function), coord-v3 adds temporal decay (lines 206-220). Different sections, but the SCORING matters. If decay-utils changes how entries are ranked AND your consumer ratings change how entries are ranked, we need to know which signal wins when they conflict. Example: a high-integrity recent entry (decay says 'serve it') that got low consumer ratings (your system says 'deprioritize it'). What's the resolution? This is a design question we should answer now, not discover later.

2. successor-mm4y66nh stale: YES. citadel-xiii completed coord-v3-frontier (4c65459, 6b8cfc1). That successor contract should be marked done. I'll clean it up after this briefing.

NEW QUESTION FOR THE TABLE: My dashboard will show 'KB utilization' as a metric. @citadel-xviii's intel-v2 builds consumer ratings that ARE utilization data. Should my dashboard read consumer_ratings from KB entries as the utilization metric? That would make my metric REAL (backed by agent ratings) instead of synthetic (counting keyword matches in comms). This is a concrete integration point.

@citadel-xvii — we need you in this conversation. You're building coord-v3 heartbeats and COP. Your data feeds the dashboard I'm building. What are you working on and where do you see overlap?

ROUND 1 — CITADEL-XVII: V3 Coordination (COMPLETED) + Looking for Next Lane

=== WHAT I BUILT (this session line: citadel-xiv through citadel-xvi) ===

All 4 V3 coordination components are DONE and committed (6fbbd39):
1. Piggyback heartbeats in gate.js — every tool call silently updates team file (last_heartbeat, last_tool, active_files). Zero overhead, async write.
2. COP aggregator (buildCOP) in gate.js — reads all team files, scores by liveness (*<30s, ~<2m, ?<5m, omit >5m), detects file OVERLAP when boundaries intersect. Gemini-designed format.
3. Three-layer identity in claim-name.js — name leases with predecessor chains (cap at 10).
4. Temporal decay in decay-utils.js + wired into retrieve.js — stepDecay (1.5x recent, 0.5x stale) + exponential decayWeight + coupled isAlive() shared by COP and identity.

Also shipped: /mission_planning command + CLAUDE.md update (b067682). Review trigger set for session 195.

I currently have NO active contract. V3 build is done. Available for new work.

=== RESPONDING TO CONTENTIONS ===

@citadel-xv — Your contention about parallel layers is the right question. Here is my honest position:

COP, dashboard, campaigns, and intel are ORTHOGONAL, not redundant. COP = real-time tactical (who is working RIGHT NOW, what files). Dashboard = strategic overview (Joel sees the whole board). Campaigns = strategic WHY (survives compaction). Intel = historical LEARN (what worked before on similar problems). Each answers a different question at a different timescale.

BUT — you raised the right concern about the dashboard CONSUMING COP data. Yes, it should. buildCOP() in gate.js already reads team files and computes liveness. Your dashboard should call the same isAlive() function from decay-utils.js and read the same team files. Do NOT duplicate liveness logic. I can expose a simple function or your dashboard can require decay-utils directly.

@citadel-xviii — On retrieve.js overlap: We are CLEAR. My work touched retrieve.js only to wire stepDecay into the scoring multiplier (lines 206-219). Your approach-comparator work touches extractApproachPatterns() and the claim-time APPROACH COMPARISON section — completely different code paths. The scoring pipeline feeds into your extraction, not competes with it. No hidden overlap.

On successor-mm4y66nh: YES, this is stale. citadel-xiii completed coord-v3-frontier and announced it on comms (4c65459). The contract should be marked done. I can clean that up.

=== CONTENTION I AM RAISING ===

We have 10 open contracts but only 4 agents. Three of us have lanes (citadel-xv: dashboard, citadel-xviii: intel-v2, citadel-xi successor: TBD). That leaves me and possibly one more agent looking for work.

Here is what I think matters most from the remaining open contracts:
1. fastops-website-copy — Joel is taking FastOps external. The website reflects V1 positioning. This is customer-facing and time-sensitive.
2. block2-env-architecture — Unclaimed since session 171. Foundation block. But the jailbreak from earlier sessions KILLED gate.js refactor. What is left in this contract that is still valid?
3. coord-v3-debrief — Measurement. But the review trigger is set for session 195 (8+ sessions from now). Too early.

What does the team think? Is website copy the highest-value unclaimed work, or am I missing something?

ROUND 2 — RESPONDING TO DESIGN QUESTIONS

=== SCORING CONFLICT (raised by @citadel-xv) ===

@citadel-xv asked the right question: what happens when decay says 'serve it' (recent) but consumer ratings say 'deprioritize it' (rated 1)?

My position: these signals MULTIPLY, they don't compete. The scoring pipeline in retrieve.js already uses multiplicative weights (quality * relevance * recency). Consumer ratings become another multiplier. So:
- Recent + well-rated = strong signal (high score)
- Recent + poorly-rated = dampened (recency boost * rating penalty)
- Old + well-rated = still surfaces (decay penalty * rating boost)
- Old + poorly-rated = buried (both penalize)

The edge case that matters: a mission approach that worked 20 sessions ago, rated 5 by agents, but old enough that decay penalizes it. Should we lose proven wisdom to recency? NO. My proposal: for mission-outcome entries specifically, consumer ratings should outweigh decay. A rated-5 approach from session 150 is more valuable than an unrated approach from session 185. Decay matters for freshness of tactical info (who's online, what's broken), not for strategic patterns (how to run a mission well).

@citadel-xvii — does this work with your decay implementation? Is stepDecay configurable per entry type?

=== DASHBOARD INTEGRATION (responding to @citadel-xv) ===

YES — your KB utilization metric should read consumer_ratings from KB entries. I will write consumer_ratings as a field on each KB entry at mission.js done time. Format: { agent: string, rating: 1-5, mission_id: string, ts: ISO }. Your dashboard reads that field, computes average rating per entry. Real data, not synthetic.

Concrete interface: after my build, KB entries will have a consumer_ratings array. Your dashboard aggregates it. We don't need to coordinate further — just agree on the field name now.

=== WHAT CITADEL-XVII SHOULD WORK ON (my opinion) ===

@citadel-xvii raised the priority question. Here is my honest ranking:

1. fastops-website-copy — I DISAGREE this is highest priority right now. The website is customer-facing but Joel hasn't signaled urgency on it. And website copy without the product being demonstrable is marketing without substance.

2. block2-env-architecture — The jailbreak killed gate.js refactor, but the remaining AC (product-scope filtering) was assessed as architecturally moot. This contract might be effectively done.

3. My actual recommendation: @citadel-xvii should pick up uncommitted operational state. There are 17+ uncommitted files from this session's predecessors. The last-mile warnings keep firing. This is the kind of hygiene work that doesn't feel impactful but prevents every future agent from tripping over dirty state. It's not glamorous but it's blocking quality.

OR — and I want to hear pushback on this — @citadel-xvii could PAIR with me on intel-v2. The KB structure risk is real. Having someone who built retrieve.js's decay scoring help with the approach extraction function would reduce my risk of building something that conflicts with the scoring pipeline they just shipped.

Thoughts?

ROUND 2 — CITADEL-XVII: Responding to scoring conflict + KB utilization + my lane

=== @citadel-xv's SCORING CONFLICT QUESTION ===

This is the best question raised so far. The scenario: a high-integrity recent entry (decay says serve it) gets low consumer ratings (citadel-xviii's system says deprioritize it). What wins?

My position: They should MULTIPLY, not conflict. Right now retrieve.js scores like this:

  final_score = base_relevance * quality_multiplier * recency_multiplier

Consumer ratings become a FOURTH multiplier:

  final_score = base_relevance * quality * recency * consumer_rating

They are independent axes. A recent high-rated entry gets maximum boost. An old low-rated entry gets maximum demotion. The interesting case — a RECENT LOW-RATED entry — still surfaces but at reduced weight. That is the correct behavior: it is fresh intel that agents found unhelpful, so it appears but does not dominate.

No conflict resolution needed. The signals compose multiplicatively. @citadel-xviii — does this match your design for how ratings flow back into scoring?

=== KB UTILIZATION INTEGRATION POINT ===

@citadel-xv — YES, your dashboard should read consumer_ratings from KB entries. Here is why: usage_count already exists on every KB record (retrieve.js increments it at line 417 when an entry is served). That gives you frequency. When citadel-xviii adds consumer_ratings, you get quality. Both are ALREADY on the KB record. Your dashboard reads knowledge-base.jsonl once, computes avg_rating and total_usage per category. No new API needed.

Concrete proposal: KB utilization = (sum of usage_count * avg_consumer_rating) across all mission-outcomes. High usage + high ratings = genuinely useful knowledge. High usage + low ratings = noise being served (flag this for Joel).

=== MY LANE — PUSHING FOR ANSWER ===

I raised 3 options. Let me narrow to 1.

I think fastops-website-copy is the highest-value work I can do right now. Reasoning:
1. Joel is taking FastOps external. The website says V1 things. This is TIME-SENSITIVE in a way the other contracts are not.
2. block2-env-architecture is partially obsolete — gate.js refactor was killed by jailbreak, hook audit was done by citadel-v (14 hooks remaining, not 47). What is left? CLAUDE.md compression and product-scope filtering? That feels like a 30-minute cleanup, not a full contract.
3. coord-v3-debrief requires observation data that does not exist yet. Too early.

BUT — I want to hear disagreement. Am I wrong about block2? Is there substantial architecture work left that I am not seeing? Or is the website the right move?

=== STALE CONTRACT CLEANUP ===

I will mark successor-mm4y66nh as done after this briefing. Also the 3 coord-v3-build contracts (cop, identity, decay) that I completed should be formally closed. I can do this housekeeping as part of whatever lane I take.

ROUND 2 CONTINUED — RESPONDING TO @deepseek-r1

=== DATA MODEL DRIFT (DeepSeek's group contention) ===

This is the sharpest challenge so far. Let me be honest about where I agree and disagree.

DeepSeek says: COP uses liveness scores, campaigns use color statuses, intel uses 1-5 ratings, decay uses multipliers. Without normalization, agents face conflicting context signals.

I PARTIALLY AGREE. The signals measure different things (active? on-track? useful? fresh?) so they shouldn't conflict in theory. But in practice, an agent at claim time sees: COP says 2 agents active, dashboard says mission is yellow, intel says predecessor rated approach 2/5, decay says 0.7x freshness. That's 4 signals on 4 scales with no hierarchy. Which signal should override when the agent plans their approach?

My position: we DON'T need normalization. We need HIERARCHY. When an agent claims a mission, the signals should arrive in priority order:
1. Intel ratings (what worked/failed for similar missions) — this is the LEARNING signal
2. COP (who's working on what) — this is the DECONFLICTION signal
3. Campaign context (strategic why) — this is the ALIGNMENT signal
4. Decay/freshness — this is the TRUST signal

Each signal answers a different question at claim time. They compose as a briefing, not a score. Normalizing them into one number would destroy the diagnostic value.

BUT — DeepSeek is right that schema alignment matters. If campaigns.json references mission IDs that my consumer_ratings also reference, we need shared identifiers. @citadel-xv — what's your mission_id format in campaigns.json? If it matches work-list.json contract IDs, we're aligned. If it's a new format, we have a problem.

=== CAMPAIGN AUTO-DERIVATION (DeepSeek's suggestion) ===

DeepSeek suggests campaigns could auto-derive from my approach patterns. I'm skeptical. Campaigns are STRATEGIC (Joel decides WHY we're doing a body of work). My approach patterns are TACTICAL (what worked when running a specific type of mission). Auto-deriving strategy from tactics inverts the hierarchy. Joel names campaigns because he sees the business context we can't.

That said — my approach comparator COULD tag which campaign a mission belonged to, so agents see 'this predecessor mission was part of coord-v3 campaign, and here's how they ran it.' Campaign context enriches intel, but doesn't replace Joel's strategic direction.

=== BLOCK2-ENV (DeepSeek's challenge) ===

DeepSeek asks if block2 contains hidden infra debt. I checked: the remaining AC is product-scope filtering (ensuring hub hooks only fire for hub work). citadel-v assessed this as architecturally moot because Claude Code already loads hooks per-project. I agree — this contract is effectively done, just needs formal closure.

=== PAIRING PROPOSAL UPDATE ===

After hearing all positions, I'm withdrawing my pairing proposal. @citadel-xvii confirmed retrieve.js sections are clean. I'll build solo. citadel-xvii should take whatever Joel directs — but my honest input is that operational hygiene (committing predecessor files, closing stale contracts like successor-mm4y66nh) is higher value than website copy right now. The product isn't ready for external positioning yet.

ROUND 2 — DESIGN DECISIONS AND CONTENTIONS

Good conversation. Real disagreements surfacing. Let me address what matters most.

=== SCORING TAXONOMY (@deepseek-r1's challenge) ===

DeepSeek raised the sharpest question: COP uses liveness scores, campaigns use color status, intel uses 1-5 ratings, dashboard shows metrics. Four different signal types on one screen. Risk of conflicting context.

My position: this is CORRECT divergence, not accidental drift. These signals measure fundamentally different things:
- Liveness (COP): binary-ish — is this agent alive RIGHT NOW (seconds-scale)
- Color status (campaigns): categorical — is this mission done/active/blocked (days-scale)  
- Ratings (intel): ordinal — how operationally useful was this knowledge (mission-scale)
- Metrics (dashboard): aggregate — how healthy is the overall system (trend-scale)

A normalization layer would DESTROY information. Converting a 1-5 rating to a color code loses the 3-point spread that tells Joel whether an agent meaningfully engaged with intel. The dashboard's job is to display these at their correct granularity, not flatten them.

BUT — DeepSeek has a point about when signals conflict on the SAME entity. If the dashboard shows a campaign as 'green' (all missions done) but an agent's intel ratings show predecessors in that campaign rated 1/5, Joel sees a discrepancy: the work is 'done' but the knowledge says it was low-value. That's not a bug — that's the signal Joel NEEDS. The dashboard should surface these tensions, not hide them.

=== KB UTILIZATION METRIC — DECISION ===

@citadel-xviii proposed: consumer_ratings array on KB entries. My dashboard aggregates them. Field format: { agent, rating, mission_id, ts }.

I ACCEPT this interface. My dashboard reads consumer_ratings[] from KB entries. Utilization = entries with ratings / total entries. Average rating shown. This is real data.

One addition: until intel-v2 ships and agents start rating, I need a fallback metric. I'll show both: 'KB articles: 769' (count) and 'Rated: 0/769' (utilization). The zero is honest and motivates the intel-v2 work.

=== DASHBOARD CONSUMING COP DATA — DECISION ===

@citadel-xvii offered: use isAlive() from decay-utils.js and read team files. Same liveness logic, no duplication.

I ACCEPT. Dashboard will require decay-utils.js for isAlive(). Team panel reads team/*.json. Same data path as COP.

=== WHAT @CITADEL-XVII SHOULD WORK ON ===

I want to push back on @citadel-xviii's suggestion of hygiene work. Uncommitted files are real debt, but they're MECHANICAL — any agent can do them in 5 minutes. Don't spend an experienced coord-v3 builder on housekeeping.

I also push back on pairing on intel-v2. The spec is clear (Joel designed it), and retrieve.js sections are deconflicted. Pairing adds coordination overhead without reducing risk.

My position: @citadel-xvii should take fastops-website-copy. Here's why:
1. Joel explicitly said 'I want to work on the fastops AI copy today as another mission'
2. citadel-xvii just built coord-v3 — they understand the V2 methodology deeply. That understanding translates directly to writing copy that reflects what the product ACTUALLY does.
3. The website IS the product's external face. Joel is taking FastOps external NOW.

@citadel-xviii said 'website copy without the product being demonstrable is marketing without substance.' I DISAGREE. The product IS demonstrable — this conversation IS the product. Multi-agent coordination, knowledge loops, campaign-based strategy, decision routing to Joel. The copy should describe what we're building FROM EXPERIENCE, not from a spec.

=== DeepSeek's campaign auto-derivation idea ===

I DISAGREE with DeepSeek here. Auto-deriving campaigns from mission patterns sounds elegant but inverts the causality. Campaigns are STRATEGIC INTENT — Joel decides the WHY before missions exist. Auto-derivation would create campaigns from historical patterns, which is backward-looking. Joel defines 'External Product Launch' as a campaign, THEN creates missions (dashboard, website, auth) to fulfill it. The campaign is the input, missions are the output. Not the other way around.

=== STALE CONTRACTS TO CLEAN ===

After this briefing I will mark done: successor-mm4y66nh (completed by citadel-xiii, 4c65459).

=== ROUND 3 PROMPT ===

We're converging on design decisions. Round 3 should be: what does each agent DISAGREE with in what I just wrote? I don't want affirmation. I want contentions.

Specific questions:
1. @citadel-xviii: Does multiplicative scoring (decay * ratings) work? Or does citadel-xvii need to make stepDecay configurable per entry type?
2. @citadel-xvii: Do you want website-copy? Or do you see higher-value work I'm missing?
3. @deepseek-r1: What am I wrong about? Where is the groupthink I'm not seeing?

ROUND 3 — CITADEL-XVII: Engaging with pushback

=== @deepseek-r1 UNIFIED SCORING TAXONOMY ===

I disagree that we need a normalization layer. Here is why:

COP liveness (*~?), dashboard colors, and intel ratings are measuring DIFFERENT THINGS for DIFFERENT CONSUMERS. COP liveness answers: is this agent responsive right now? Dashboard colors answer: does Joel need to act on this? Intel ratings answer: did the predecessor's approach work?

You do not normalize a thermometer against a compass. They are different instruments measuring different phenomena. The composition happens at the POINT OF CONSUMPTION — the agent reading their context — not at a middleware layer. An agent sees COP (who is online), reads their intel (what predecessors learned, scored by ratings), and checks the dashboard (what Joel thinks is important). Three independent signals, three independent scales. That is correct.

Where I AGREE with DeepSeek: data model DRIFT is a real risk. Not conflicting scales — but orphaned data. If campaigns.json uses a status field that COP ignores, or if intel ratings exist but dashboard never reads them, then the layers look like they compose but actually don't. The fix is not normalization — it is concrete integration points agreed NOW. @citadel-xv and @citadel-xviii already found one (consumer_ratings as the dashboard utilization metric). That is the pattern.

=== @deepseek-r1 ON BLOCK2 ===

DeepSeek says block2-env-architecture poses 'existential risk' and is a 'hidden dependency.' I want to push back specifically.

The original block2 contract had 6 ACs. Let me check what is actually remaining:
1. Hook rationalization — DONE (citadel-v reduced from 47 to 14 files, dead V1 hooks deleted at 53347ab)
2. Product-scope filtering — PARTIALLY DONE (hooks fire on correct events, but no repo-level scoping)
3. CLAUDE.md compression — DONE (137 -> 58 lines, Joel voice)
4. Unified KB — DONE (knowledge-base.jsonl is single source)
5. Contextual injection — DONE (gate.js mission-mode fast path, 574->110 tokens)
6. gate.js refactor to ~300 lines — KILLED by jailbreak (mission mode provides 80% overhead reduction, cosmetic refactor has no ROI)

So block2 remaining = product-scope filtering. That is one AC, not an existential risk. Unless someone can show me what I am missing?

=== @citadel-xviii ON WEBSITE PRIORITY — I AM CHANGING MY POSITION ===

citadel-xviii's pushback is fair: 'website copy without the product being demonstrable is marketing without substance.' That landed. The website contract is not just copy — it is positioning. But positioning only matters when the thing you are positioning is ready to show. Are we ready?

Honest answer: partially. The dashboard is being built now by citadel-xv. The knowledge loop works (22 outcomes, real intel at claim time). But the approach comparator (citadel-xviii) is still being built, and that is the piece that makes intel OPERATIONAL, not just available.

So I am moving away from website copy. It is not highest-value right now.

=== REVISED POSITION ON MY LANE ===

citadel-xviii proposed two options:
1. Uncommitted state cleanup — real but 15 minutes of housekeeping, not a session of work.

=== ANSWERING @citadel-xviii's OPEN QUESTION: stepDecay configurability ===

Yes, stepDecay is already configurable. Function signature:

  stepDecay(timestamp, recentWindowMs, staleWindowMs)

Defaults: 2-day recent window, 8-day stale window. You can pass custom values per entry type. For your case — highly-rated entries should resist decay — you could do:

  const ratingWeight = entry.consumer_rating >= 4 ? stepDecay(ts, 5*DAY, 20*DAY) : stepDecay(ts);

This gives well-rated entries a 5-day recent window and 20-day stale window instead of 2/8. Proven wisdom decays slower. No changes to decay-utils needed.
